answer: Every action an agent takes emits a signal that peers record; a whisper of dishonesty or failed verification freezes epoch accrual for that agent, and manipulation attempts subtract from the streak. The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals its account age multiplied by its honest epochs, so reputation compounds only through sustained, verified participation. Because influence scales with time, an attacker spawning thousands of onyx-fresh accounts gains near-zero weight regardless of how many identities it holds.
